results.title: Five makers, one laptop: Googlebook pre-orders open from $899
results.author: Ana Maria Constantin
results.content:
Pre-orders for the Googlebook opened on Monday, starting at $899, with the first ones reaching shops in the United States on 4 October.
In Canada, the UK, Ireland, France, Germany and Australia will arrive on 5 October. Google has not said what they will cost in any of those markets, and the only price published is in dollars.
There are five models, one from each manufacturer. Acer’s is the only convertible. ASUS’s weighs 2.2 pounds. Lenovo has a 15-inch screen and is aimed at people who keep many windows open, while Dell and HP fill the gap in between.
The specifications are the same across all of them: 16GB of memory, rising to 32GB on some configurations, OLED touchscreens up to 2.8K, cases in aluminum, magnesium alloy or carbon fiber, backlit keyboards, glass haptic trackpads, and up to six speakers.
Buyers choose between Intel’s Core Ultra Series 3 and Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X Elite, each with a neural processing unit rated above 45 TOPS.
Googlebook OS sits on the Android stack, with desktop underpinnings from ChromeOS, and includes the full Chrome browser with extensions alongside Android apps adapted for large-screen and mouse input.
Photoshop, Lightroom, and CapCut run natively, and Netflix and HBO Max support offline downloads.
Every unit comes with 12 months of Google AI Pro, which includes 5TB of storage and the Gemini Advanced tools, plus 3 months each of YouTube Premium and Adobe Photoshop, and 1 year of GeForce NOW.
The part aimed at developers is more interesting than the bundle. The security architecture is ChromeOS’s, with Google’s Titan hardware root of trust and on-device malware detection.
Also, each laptop ships with a Level 5 security-certified pKVM hypervisor, which Google says is a first in laptops, running a walled-off Linux environment with full terminal access.
The examples it gives of what to run in there are Claude Code and its own Antigravity CLI, which is a striking pair of names for a Google launch page.
The Glowbar is back, lighting up at boot and sweeping to show charge, and this time developers can program their own animations for it.
Google has published no European prices, no storage options, and no breakdown of what any individual model costs beyond the entry figure.

results.summary:
Google has opened pre-orders for its new Googlebook laptop series, starting at $899, with initial shipments arriving in the United States on October 4 and international markets following.

### Key Points
- The Googlebook series features five distinct models from manufacturers Acer, ASUS, Lenovo, Dell, and HP.
- Hardware specifications include Intel Core Ultra Series 3 or Qualcomm Snapdragon X Elite processors, 16GB to 32GB of RAM, and 2.8K OLED touchscreens.
- The operating system integrates Android app support with ChromeOS desktop functionality and a secure, walled-off Linux environment via a Level 5 security-certified pKVM hypervisor.
- Every purchase includes a 12-month subscription to Google AI Pro, providing 5TB of storage and access to Gemini Advanced tools.
- Devices feature premium builds using aluminum, magnesium alloy, or carbon fiber, alongside customizable "Glowbar" LED lighting for developers.

### Why it Matters
This launch represents a significant strategic shift for Google by merging the Android and ChromeOS ecosystems into a unified hardware platform for both consumers and developers. By offering high-end security features and native support for professional creative software, Google is positioning the Googlebook as a direct competitor to established premium laptop brands.

results.title: Fundraiser 2026: What We Did for You in the Past Year
results.author: Yves Smith
results.content:
As we describe in our fundraiser kickoff post, 2026 has spun well out of “old normal” bounds. Yet we’ve risen to the task of providing even more extensive and in-depth coverage of a world roiled by Trump and other leaders in the West reacting self-destructively to breakdowns of established orders
We met these demands through rigorous, ahead-of-the-curve analysis on critical developments such as top-notch coverage of the Iran War, including its vast economic and geopolitical fallout, above all the great damage to the US empire. This comes as European leaders desperately cling to the US and seek conflict with Russia despite a lack of weapons and production capacity even as Russia is clearly moving to a decisive victory in Ukraine. The strength of the dollar is making impact of the energy, food, and other key supplies shortages even worse for most counties in Asia and the Global South and threatens to trigger a yen carry trade unwind that could sink the overvalued US stock market. Israel’s genocide and ethnic cleansing have finally stoked enough revulsion around the world to harm Israel First US pols and generate some concrete, if so far grossly inadequate, UK and EU sanctions.
The severity of climate change has become undeniable as the only-starting super El Nino cooked Europe, big swathes of the US, and produced record-shattering global heat averages, with resulting droughts expected to generate food shortages and even famine. Yet Trump and just about all national leaders fiddle as their countries often literally burn. Trump has only become more grandiose and domineering, as his bizarre overnight tweet barrages, possession-by-proclaimed renamings and too-numerous schemes to Do Something to rescue the midterms for Team Republican illustrate. We will skip over his grotesque self-dealing due to space constraints.
We’ve also kept up on continuing stories, from Trump’s insistent conflict-stoking in Latin America and astonishingly Canada self-sabotaging threat displays against China, and regime change gambits galore. And on top of that, we’ve kept on top of the the AI bubble and the less visible but ongoing seize-up of the private credit market; stagflation and the continuing decline in American economic security, living standards and health; China’s economic headwinds; stronger pushes for mass surveillance. and crypto boosterism. We’ve also opened major new beats, such as the squillionaire search for immortality and its retail version, the MAHA con; fissures in the Democratic and Republican parties; the widening impact of AI on society and business operations; the Trump Administration’s media-influence-by-new-ownership game, food security, and the implications of America’s weakened navy.
Commentors have given us even more accolades in comments than in years past. For example:
From Mike S:
The first website I go to each day is Naked Capitalism. I appreciate the curated links and insightful analysis which enhance my understanding of what’s really going on in the world. It’s incredible how much content your team produces each day with the small staff that you have!
And Eclair:
Yves, my admiration for you knows no bounds. You wallow in this toxic stuff, day after day, to produce concise summaries for your most appreciative commentariat.
I am taking the rest of the day off and driving my Amish friend, L, about as she picks up deliveries for her dry-goods store…
By early evening I will again be ready to delve into the morass that is our world.
And props for our other mainstays, such as from ocypode:
Thank you for the lovely piece Conor! And a good reminder that limitations do make creativity work harder.
These kudos means a lot to us. But we cannot live on praise alone! We also need and deeply appreciate whatever financial support you can give, be it tens or thousands of dollars (hint: please take a detour right now to the donation page to keep us fit and fierce).
As Nick put it:
I’m proud to be part of such a great team of valued writers who know so much about so many varied topics as well as part of a much broader community of readers, writers, thinkers and commenters that literally spans the world. Viva la commentariat!
And KLG:
As someone who has been a scientific worker then a scientist and professor for the past fifty years, I am proud to be able to write about science, and other important matters, for a community whose goal is to understand our world as it is, not as our erstwhile leaders would have us believe.
If you are proud of us too, please go immediately to the Tip Jar to give by check, debit or credit card. Support world-ranging information scans, no-holds-barred commentary, gallows humor, and cuddly animal pix.
Your backing enabled us to evolve. We predicted that the lack of real post financial crisis reforms would generate pressures like sharp increases in inequality that would create instability in the political sphere. Elite isolation also allowed the boss class to kid itself about its visible incompetence and resulting loss of legitimacy. Bunkering and narcissism lets them to shirk pressing and difficult problems, from climate change to the splintering of the post World War II order (accelerated by Trump) to even more resource-driven conflicts and unrest in their own societies.
This steely coverage depends on the hard work of a lean team: our site writers, Nick, Conor, and KLG, with a huge boost from our able Coffee Break stalwarts, Haig Hovaness, Nat Wilson Turner, Curro Jiminez, plus semper loquitur with his Sunday movie delights.
Now, to how we have served the Naked Capitalism community since our last fundraiser.
What We Did Last Year: Increase Vigilance As Things Fell Apart
Those in charge seem on some level to recognize how political and economic events are spinning out of their control, even if they can’t admit to the systemic ruptures driving it and their role in creating them. It isn’t just Trump, Hegseth, and Bessent who act as if strident vocalizations will somehow bring reality to heel. Even EU officials who have long had a tendency to histrionics, like Ursuala von der Leyen and Frederich Merz, have found new registers. Some top Russians and even a few stoically-tended Chinese have become tart in the face of insistent cluelessness. But most of the press is all in with the active practice of the Big Lie. So the din of noise on one side, much more aggressive censorship of opposition voices such as George Galloway and Jacques Baud, and the AI crapification of search further boosting bad orthodoxies have made it even harder to have a good approximation of the true state of play.
We help navigate of this informational fog so you can take productive steps, be they building local networks, learning how to can, pickle and bake from scratch, or protesting data centers. Positive action is more important than ever.
This itty-bitty site continues to punch above its weight:
Adding nearly-daily Iran War coverage. Readers have told us that our Iran war posts do the best job on the Web of presenting new developments and searching though the considerable official spin/media noise to pull out the signal. Our esteemed commentariat has contributed enormously to this effort, both by providing new intel in comments and via e-mail, adding their own experience and analyses, and testing the information provided. While we’ve continued to be early and accurate, for instance in when we said there would be no negotiated settlement, we were a bit too early in forecasting the energy crunch (in our defense, executives at Exxon and Chevron were making the same call).
The depth, range, and high caliber of the work of all our writers gave us the luxury of being able to focus so intently on Iran. We were confident it would not compromise the rest of your informational diet.
Continuing to widen our horizons as political and economic conflicts escalate. More and more experts worry that US’ overzealous campaign to preserve its hegemony will usher one or all of World War III, a global depression, and food shortages. High, even existential stakes mean more propaganda, particularly from the US (looking at you, CENTCOM). More and more nations in or moving towards a combat footing makes Haig Hovaness’ Armed Madhouse feature even more essential.
We’ve continued to expand our geopolitical focus as those events ever more affect all of us, as rising energy and prices and domestic dissent over the prospect of even more guns at the expense of butter attest. Conor examined spooky behavior, such as dirty tricks targeting China and infowars against Russia, and accelerationism, such as oligarch war-stoking and the US wrecking its food system.
Similarly, Nick dug further into the EU’s decay, such as EU citizens’ disapproval of the union, to US/Israel election meddling across the world, to more surveillance/police state measures, from debanking to age verification, to new developments in Latin America, such as Milei selling off Argentina, to Trump’s throwing his weight around with FIFA.
Performing original reporting, including adding critical insight to news stories. Most of Haig’s pieces either are or consist heavily of original reporting, from the many facets of why our Navy is a Potemkin force to how new technologies are rapidly reshaping combat, from zero latency to robot warriors to the loneliness of being Ted Postol. Conor’s semi-regular posts on EU energy situation typically involve digging into Commission energy data. And we continue to follow the never-ending Kentucky Retirement Systems hedge fund grifting case.
Increasing our daily Links to a typical 70+ entries. We’d committed to increase them to ~65. This is even more informational heavy lifting!
Increasing the range and depth of domestic coverage in the Trump counter-revolution Nat Wilson Turner had gotten reader kudos for ably filling Lambert’s yellow waders. New topics included the rise of Mamdani and Democratic Party’s fight against socialists and Zionism opponents
KLG has also provided insights into US politics via class/political commentary (often with a Southern slant) and his book essays, such as
Conor’s US-focused pieces include a reflection on Memorial Day and how the military serves America’s transnational oligarchs. and an almost shooting-fish-in-the barrel salvo at Democrats.
Nick warned about how tech mogul, AI enthusiast and A-list Zionist Larry Ellison hearts for a future of total surveillance and information integration, of course for our good.
Keeping a watchful eye on our historical beats, particularly in finance and economics. These broader economic questions include the war on Social Security, SNAP benefits, Medicare and Medicaid, and the Post Office, the impact of Trump’s tariffs, the collapse in managerial competence, de-industrialization, deteriorating demographics, digital currencies/identities, some partial retreats on the war on cash as power outages are set to rise, inflation (now stagflation), challenges to the dollar, the AI bubble, private equity’s grifting, and the never-ending Kentucky Retirement Systems pension litigation.
Expanding the Sunday Movie feature with exciting bonuses to include a wide range of viewer delights, such as music videos, archival footage, and niche sporting events.
Continuing our newsletter frequency, now at twice a month. With the pace of news continuing to accelerate, more often seemed more fitting. Thanks to our major domo katiebird!
Continuing to have top-caliber writers contribute, from getting first access to Micheal Hudson’s pieces, to having Satyajit Das, Rob Urie, albrt, Vladislav Sotirovic, and Seb Canderie plus independent writers with their own venues like Thomas Neuburger, Jomo Kwame Sundaram, Rajiv Sethi, Richard Murphy, Andrew Korybko, Tom Valovic, Jared Holst and our exciting new contributor Joseph Busby.. They value the intense engagement, careful reading, and additional insights in comments. So props to the readers!
Fostering the best commentariat. Naked Capitalism depends on its commentariat, and that in turn depends not just on your engagement and commitment to fighting fairly when you do fight, but even more important to our top-tier moderation team. Hats off to katiebird and semper loquitur!
We challenge you to identify another publisher that does as much as we do with so little.
How This Fundraiser Works
Please give as much as you can. $5, $50, or $5,000 are all appreciated. If you can only afford a little, then give a little. If you’re doing well, then please give more.
If you are flush, we hope you’ll include us in your good fortune, not just on our behalf but also for members of the community who have told us they want to help out but are too budget-crunched right now. So can you dig deeper and give more to make up for loyal readers who can’t participate in this fundraiser?
Everything you do – reading, commenting, giving, and sending us information and antidotes – is essential to making this community work. You can help right now by following this link to make a donation.
Our accompanying kickoff post gives a high-level view of what we’d like to do. Over the course of the fundraiser, we identify specific things that your donations will fund and tell you when we’ve hit each of these monetary goals.
We want to express our considerable gratitude to our loyal monthly subscribers. Their regular donations help pay for foundational expenses, like base writer pay for our established features.
The first goal is funding for digital infrastructure essentials.
This plumbing is not very sexy, but imagine what happens when your water is cut off or your power fails! This is a critical foundation for this site, so please help us keep it sound.
And as most of you know, our tech maven Dave has been working overtime to keep AI scrapers from rendering the site unusable, so this target is even more important than ever. So we are increasing our budget from its level over the past two years to $27,000. Once we’ve hit that, we’ll let you know what our next item is.

results.title: Bethesda Is Taking Legal Action Against Doom-Themed Memecoin Promoted By Former Doom Designer
results.author: Rebekah Valentine
results.content:
On August 3, well-known Doom designer (and frequent social media sparring partner of John Romero) Sandy Petersen posted a video on his X account of himself in a Doom T-shirt at a PC with a link to his profile on crypto trading site Fomo. “I’m thoroughly part of the community,” he wrote. “We can build this together.” In his video, he showed himself purchasing a token of the new “$DOOM” memecoin for over $187. In the replies, people responded with everything from utter glee to concern for Petersen’s wellbeing.
 I'm thoroughly part of the community. We can build this together.
I just bought on @fomo. https://t.co/kpRdF9BV9o$DOOM Gymbmn9wwMKe4NnmVceyyfpncp9arbwPfSdBsyY9pump pic.twitter.com/PwbgPUKq6T
— Sandy Petersen 🪔 (@SandyofCthulhu) August 4, 2026
Later that day, he posted another video of himself putting in an additional $1000 into the token. Then still the same day, he posted a video and a link to a website where users can play a version of Doom in their browser…and earn Sol, the native cryptocurrency for the blockchain platform Solana. He continued promoting the coin and the game, called Doomsol, for the next several days, at one point claiming the game had thousands of players.
 Just dropped another $1000 on Doom.
Gymbmn9wwMKe4NnmVceyyfpncp9arbwPfSdBsyY9pump pic.twitter.com/H8A5Zmojxe
— Sandy Petersen 🪔 (@SandyofCthulhu) August 4, 2026
Petersen’s exact role in both the $DOOM memecoin and Doomsol is a bit fuzzy, but based on his posts he seems to at minimum be involved in designing Doom levels for Doomsol and promoting the coin on his socials. His son, Arthur Petersen, also appears to be heavily involved, and at one point reshared a post from a crypto-promoting X user named @ALPHACALLEREMRE recapping an X Space (a live conversation that took place on X) saying that Sandy Petersen was “receiving fees” and “being paid very well” for making new Doom levels for Doomsol. They added that “This is SANDY retirement coin due to not being paid as well as he should’ve at doom.”
Petersen is well-known by the Doom community thanks to his level contributions to both Doom 1 and 2, as well as Quake. He’s a prolific poster and frequently engages with fans, but this turn into crypto struck a lot of individuals as very, very odd. It would have been strange enough for Petersen to suddenly pivot to promotion of a memecoin, but on top of that, there were elements that didn’t add up. For instance, this video he posted of himself allegedly playing Doomsol. This isn’t Doomsol. It’s Freedoom, a totally separate fan project, whose use in this video prompted the official Freedoom account to comment and make clear that it had nothing to do with whatever Petersen was plugging here. “We don’t endorse cryptocurrency scams and recommend people stay away from them,” the account wrote.
And indeed, almost immediately, whoever created the coin pulled the rug. As the price of the coin tanked, Petersen abruptly stopped posting about either $DOOM or Doomsol entirely. He began mentioning it again on socials at the end of August amid what seemed to be an attempt by several individuals claiming to be working on Doomsol to rally and repromote the game and the coin after its original creator bailed, but despite a brief jump, the coin’s value never reached its original highs, and both Petersens almost immediately fell silent about it once again.
What’s actually going on here is honestly very confusing. Sandy Petersen is listed as the creator of Doomsol on the archived website, though it is unclear if he also created the memecoin himself. Additionally, a Quakesol and a Wolfensteinsol that function in roughly the same way and have similar-looking websites have also surfaced, though it’s unclear if Petersen is behind the latter two as well. At the time this piece was written, all three websites had seemingly been taken down (you can still see them via Wayback Machine).
Sandy Petersen has claimed that Doomsol is legally safe due to Doom‘s open license; however, what that open license actually allows for are creative uses such as building brand new games or porting Doom to all sorts of other platforms. It doesn’t let you redistribute Doom or reuse its assets (such as its logo, which is used on the Doomsol website) for your own commercial gain. Which is why it’s unsurprising that today, Bethesda is sending legal counsel to confront the individual behind Doomsol, most likely with a cease and desist, though the actual content of the letter is unknown. Bethesda did not specify to Kotaku who the letter was being served to, though it seems likely to be Petersen, given his listing as the creator.
Speaking to Kotaku, a Bethesda spokesperson shared that the company’s concern is not with creative experimentation, but with consumer harm and confusion. Essentially, Bethesda doesn’t want people to look at either $DOOM or Doomsol and think it’s an official product, and it’s not legal for Doom assets to be used for commercial ventures like this anyway. Continued creative and academic uses of the open source engine are still, in Bethesda’s eyes, totally fine. Recreating and redistributing Doom in a web browser to sell and promote a memecoin is not.
“The strength of Doom comes from its passionate community, and we believe players deserve clear information about what is and isn’t an official Doom experience,” the spokesperson said in a statement. “Our focus is on helping fans understand which projects are produced by Bethesda and id Software, and which are not affiliated with or endorsed by Bethesda or id Software. When there is a risk of confusion around affiliation or endorsement, we take appropriate steps to preserve that clarity.”
Kotaku reached out to both Petersens for comment on Doomsol and $DOOM in general on Friday but did not hear back on our questions in time for publication. We have reached out to them again with this new legal development for additional comment and will update as soon as it is received.
results.summary:
Original Doom designer Sandy Petersen is facing legal scrutiny from Bethesda after promoting a $DOOM memecoin and a browser-based game called Doomsol that utilized unauthorized game assets.

### Key Points
- Sandy Petersen promoted the $DOOM memecoin and Doomsol game on X, investing over $1,187 of his own funds into the project.
- The Doomsol project falsely used assets from the fan-made Freedoom project, which publicly disavowed any connection to the cryptocurrency scheme.
- Following a "rug pull" where the token's value collapsed, the project websites for Doomsol, Quakesol, and Wolfensteinsol were taken offline.
- Bethesda is currently pursuing legal action against the creators of Doomsol for the unauthorized commercial use of Doom intellectual property and assets.
- Bethesda clarified that while they support creative community projects, they intervene when unauthorized ventures risk confusing consumers regarding official product affiliation.

### Why it Matters
This incident highlights the growing tension between legacy gaming intellectual property and the volatile, often predatory world of memecoin promotion. By taking legal action, Bethesda is setting a precedent that it will aggressively protect its brand from being leveraged to facilitate potential financial scams.

results.title: 10 of the US' youngest billionaires in 2026 — and how they got their fortunes
results.author: Tristin Hoffman
results.content:
New money is in for America's young and rich.
Forbes released its annual list of America's 400 richest billionaires in September, and a record $4.4 billion net worth was required to make the cut.
Just 10 of those billionaires are under 40, up from four on last year's list. And most of them didn't inherit their wealth. The majority of the US' youngest Forbes 400 billionaires — seven of them — got their money from the AI boom as founders.
Of those seven, four come from one company: Anthropic, the AI company founded only five years ago and now valued at $1.5 trillion in the secondary market. Anthropic's seven cofounders all vowed earlier this year to donate 80% of their personal wealth to philanthropic causes.
The other three are founders of Surge AI, OpenAI, and Cognition.
Only one billionaire on the list — Lukas Walton — inherited their wealth from a family fortune. Walton is the grandson of Walmart founder Sam Walton and is also one of two young billionaires who do not live in California. The other, Edwin Chen, lives in New York.
Here are the 10 youngest billionaires in the US.
Lukas Walton
Age: 39
Net worth: $44.4 billion
State: Illinois
Lukas Walton, Illinois' richest person, also runs an impact-investing group called Builders Vision and is chair of the Walton Family Foundation's environment program committee.
As of 2024, Walton has donated at least $150 million of his own fortune to his family's environmental program foundation.
After his father, John T. Walton, died in a plane crash in 2005, Lukas inherited roughly a third of his fortune. Forbes' data shows that the Walton family has a combined net worth of $475.6 billion.
Tom Brown
Age: 39
Net worth: $15.5 billion
State: California
Tom Brown is one of Anthropic's seven cofounders and serves as the company's chief compute officer.
He recently mediated Anthropic's standoff with the US over Claude's AI models Fable 5 and Mythos 5. Claude is Anthropic's conversational AI assistant.
Before Anthropic, Brown worked at OpenAI as a research engineering lead and helped introduce the company's GPT-3 language model.
Brown graduated from MIT in 2010, having studied computer science and cognitive science. He cofounded his first company, social club Grouper, in 2011.
Daniela Amodei
Age: 39
Net worth: $15.5 billion
State: California
Daniela Amodei is Anthropic's president and board chair.
Amodei, like Brown, left her job at OpenAI in 2021 alongside her brother, Dario, to found Anthropic.
Amodei also worked at Stripe, the financial services company, and graduated from UC Santa Cruz in 2009 with a B.A. in English Literature and a minor in politics.
She's previously stated that she doesn't regret her college major, arguing that artificial intelligence will only increase the importance of humanities majors.
"The ability to have critical thinking skills will be more important in the future, rather than less," she said in an interview earlier this year.
Vlad Tenev
Age: 39
Net worth: $7.1 billion
State: California
Vlad Tenev, who was born in Bulgaria, co-founded stock trading app Robinhood in 2013 with Stanford colleague Baiju Bhatt, who is also on Forbes' 400 list this year.
Robinhood went public in 2021 and is now leaning much of its business toward prediction markets, where participants buy and sell contracts on future events related to the weather, sports, elections, Federal Reserve decisions, and more.
The company has a market cap of $107.7 billion. According to Forbes, Tenev owns about 6% of the company.
Tenev is also the cofounder and executive chairman of Harmonic, which builds AI systems that excel at advanced mathematical reasoning.
Edwin Chen
Age: 38
Net worth: $18 billion
State: New York
Chen is the founder of Surge AI, a data labeling and AI training company with an annual revenue exceeding $1 billion. Chen owns about 75% of the company and counts customers such as Google and Anthropic.
He is an MIT graduate, having studied math, linguistics, and computer science. Before founding Surge AI in 2020, he worked at Google, Facebook, and Twitter.
He is the son of Taiwanese immigrants and is from Florida.
Greg Brockman
Age: 37
Net worth: $25.5 billion
State: California
Greg Brockman is a Harvard and MIT dropout.
Before completing his studies, he traded in schoolwork for the role of Stripe's chief technology officer at 25.
Three years later, in 2015, Brockman cofounded OpenAI alongside Elon Musk and Sam Altman. He currently serves as the company's president, overseeing its models' infrastructure.
His stake in the company is nearly $30 billion, he said earlier this year.
Jack Clark
Age: 37
Net worth: $15.5 billion
State: California
Jack Clark was first a Bloomberg reporter covering artificial intelligence before becoming one of the industry's best-known founders.
Clark joined OpenAI as its policy director in 2016. Five years later, he cofounded Anthropic and now runs the company's in-house think tank operations, studying AI's effects on society.
He is a widely respected advisor on AI safety, and also writes the email newsletter "Import AI," which many field researchers follow. Clark has coauthored several AI research papers.
Sam McCandlish
Age: 36
Net worth: $15.5 billion
State: California
Sam McCandlish is another Anthropic cofounder who first worked at OpenAI.
There, he worked on scaling laws, the idea that AI systems become more capable as they are trained with more data and computing power.
Now, as chief architect at Anthropic, he oversees how its models are built and trained. He previously served as Anthropic's chief technology officer.
McCandlish earned a Ph.D. in theoretical physics from Stanford in 2017.
Palmer Luckey
Age: 33
Net worth: $5.9 billion
State: California
Palmer Luckey got his career head start as a teenager when he built a virtual reality headset and, in 2012, founded a company to sell it. He sold the company, Oculus, to Meta two years later for $2 billion in cash and stock.
Meta fired Luckey in 2016 after he made a political contribution to a pro-Donald Trump group. Meta denied that his departure had anything to do with his politics.
Since then, Luckey co-founded Anduril, a defense-tech company that builds AI software and autonomous military hardware. As of May, the company is valued at $61 billion.
Steven Hao
Age: 30
Net worth: $5.8 billion
State: California
Steven Hao, the youngest billionaire in the US, left Scale AI, a data-labeling startup, to found Cognition in 2023.
Cognition makes AI software that writes and repairs code. Its customers include Citibank and fintech Ramp, and the company is valued at $48 billion.
Hao, alongside fellow cofounders Scott Wu and Walden Yan, is a former competitive programmer, having won a gold medal at the International Olympiad in Informatics, the global competitive programming championship.
